<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan\left(-\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = -1</annotation></semantics></math> is one point; closer to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> the outputs keep falling.

why.correct: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>cos</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> undoes cosine restricted to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, \pi]</annotation></semantics></math>, so its outputs are the angles in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, \pi]</annotation></semantics></math>. The graph runs from height <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -1</annotation></semantics></math> down to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Right: the outputs are angles from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is the range of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> and (open) of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>tan</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, not of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>cos</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is the domain of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>cos</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>: the inputs are cosine values.

Cosine is not one-to-one on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 2\pi]</annotation></semantics></math> (<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\frac{\pi}{3} = \cos\frac{5\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>), so that interval cannot be the range.

why.correct: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>cos</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> is the angle in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, \pi]</annotation></semantics></math> whose cosine is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. That angle is in Quadrant II with reference angle <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi - \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{2\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

Work from the inside: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\frac{5\pi}{3} = \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. Then <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>cos</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, the angle in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, \pi]</annotation></semantics></math> with cosine <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. The inverse undoes cosine only for inputs already in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, \pi]</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Right: inner value <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, then the angle in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, \pi]</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{5\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math> is outside <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, \pi]</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>cos</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> cannot return it.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, but negative angles are outside the range of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>cos</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\frac{2\pi}{3} = -\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: Symmetry about <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> means the heights at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-x</annotation></semantics></math> average to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>cos</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos^{-1}(-0.6) = \pi - a</annotation></semantics></math>. On the unit circle, the angle with cosine <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.6</annotation></semantics></math> is the reflection of angle <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> across the <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>-axis, which is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi - a</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Right: the two outputs add to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-a</annotation></semantics></math> is negative, outside the range <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, \pi]</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos a = 0.6</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.6</annotation></semantics></math>; the inputs differ in sign, so the angles differ.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi + a</annotation></semantics></math> is greater than <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, outside the range.

why.correct: A function has an inverse only when each output comes from one input. On <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 2\pi]</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\frac{\pi}{3} = \cos\frac{5\pi}{3} = \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>: two inputs give the output <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>cos</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> would not be a single value.

Reaching <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math> is fine; the problem is outputs being repeated.

why.correct: Set up <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>0.8</mn><mn>10</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0.08</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan\theta = \frac{0.8}{10} = 0.08</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msup><mi>tan</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.08</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \tan^{-1}(0.08)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mn>0.079830</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 0.079830</annotation></semantics></math> radians (calculator in radian mode), which is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.080</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.080</annotation></semantics></math> to three decimal places.

The ratios <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mtext>rise</mtext><mtext>run</mtext></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}}</annotation></semantics></math> are <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.0833</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.0833</annotation></semantics></math> (K), <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.08</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.08</annotation></semantics></math> (L), <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.1</annotation></semantics></math> (M) and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.1125</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.1125</annotation></semantics></math> (N). <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>tan</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> is increasing, so the largest ratio gives the largest angle: ramp N, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>tan</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.1125</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.11203</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan^{-1}(0.1125) \approx 0.11203</annotation></semantics></math> radians (radian mode).

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.07</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mtext>rise</mtext><mn>10</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan(0.07) = \frac{\text{rise}}{10}</annotation></semantics></math>, so rise <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0.07</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.70114</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 10\tan(0.07) \approx 0.70114</annotation></semantics></math> meters (radian mode). Here the angle is known, so use <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>tan</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> gives the angle in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">[</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]</annotation></semantics></math> with the given sine. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, and sine is odd, so the angle is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>tan</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> gives the angle in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> with the given tangent. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan\frac{\pi}{4} = 1</annotation></semantics></math> and tangent is odd, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>tan</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan^{-1}(-1) = -\frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>.

Inside first: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\frac{3\pi}{4} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. Then <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> is the angle in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">[</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]</annotation></semantics></math> with that sine: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Right: the inner value is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, and its angle in range is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math> is outside <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">[</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> cannot return it.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> is negative; the inner value <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> is positive.

That is the inner value <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\frac{3\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>; the outer <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> turns it back into an angle.

why.correct: Write <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 2\sin x + 1</annotation></semantics></math>, swap: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2\sin y + 1</annotation></semantics></math>. Undo in reverse order: subtract <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>, divide by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>, then apply <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>sin</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{x - 1}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>. The restricted domain <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">[</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]</annotation></semantics></math> is the range of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, so this is the inverse.

The inverse functions swap the domains and ranges of the restricted functions. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> takes <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-1, 1]</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">[</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]</annotation></semantics></math>; <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>cos</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> takes <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-1, 1]</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, \pi]</annotation></semantics></math>; <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>tan</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> takes every real number to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: True: those are the angles <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> returns.

False: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, \pi]</annotation></semantics></math> is the range of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>cos</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>; its domain is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-1, 1]</annotation></semantics></math>.

True: tangent takes every real value, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>tan</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> accepts every real input.

False: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> is the inverse function, not the reciprocal; <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{\sin x}</annotation></semantics></math> is a different function.

why.correct: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>tan</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> undoes tangent on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>. The outputs are angles in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>, so they stay below <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>tan</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan^{-1}(0) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>; for large inputs the angle gets close to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> is outside the range of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>tan</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: Let <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>sin</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \sin^{-1}\frac{3}{5}</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\theta = \frac{3}{5}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">[</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]</annotation></semantics></math>; here <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> is in Quadrant I. Draw a right triangle with opposite side <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math> and hypotenuse <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math>: the adjacent side is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{25 - 9} = 4</annotation></semantics></math>. So <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\theta = \frac{4}{5}</annotation></semantics></math>, positive because <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> is in Quadrant I.
options: Right: adjacent over hypotenuse in the <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math>-<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math> triangle.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> of a positive number is an angle in Quadrant I, where cosine is positive.

Dividing both sides by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin x</annotation></semantics></math> loses the solutions where <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan x = 1</annotation></semantics></math> again at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{4} + \pi = \frac{5\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan\frac{3\pi}{4} = -1</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math> does not solve <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan x = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{5\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math> is missing.

why.correct: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos x = \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{5\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>. Test a value between them: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\pi = -1 \le \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. Test outside: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos 0 = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, too big. The endpoints count because of the <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>≤</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\le</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Right: between the two boundary angles, endpoints included.

That is where <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos x \ge \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\frac{2\pi}{3} = -\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>; the boundary values come from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos x = +\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

These are where <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos x = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sec</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sec\frac{2\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{\cos(2\pi/3)}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{-1/2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -2</annotation></semantics></math>. The graph of secant is below <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math> on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{3\pi}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>, where cosine is negative.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sec</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sec x = \frac{1}{\cos x}</annotation></semantics></math> is undefined where <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>: at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0, 2\pi]</annotation></semantics></math>. The dashed cosine crosses the axis exactly there.
options: Right: the zeros of cosine.
Those are the zeros of sine, where cosecant has its asymptotes.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sec</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sec\frac{\pi}{4} = \sqrt{2}</annotation></semantics></math> is defined.

Cosine is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> again at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, so there is a second asymptote.

why.correct: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos x</annotation></semantics></math> is between <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>, so its reciprocal has absolute value at least <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sec</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sec x \ge 1</annotation></semantics></math> where cosine is positive and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sec</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sec x \le -1</annotation></semantics></math> where it is negative. On the graph, no part of the secant curve lies strictly between <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Right: the reciprocal of a number between <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> is at least <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> in size.
That is the range of cosine; secant takes the reciprocals of those values.

Secant never takes values like <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> or <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{\cos x} = \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> would need <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos x = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

Where <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos x < 0</annotation></semantics></math>, the secant branches open downward, with outputs at most <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: Just left of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos x</annotation></semantics></math> is a small positive number, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{\cos x}</annotation></semantics></math> is a large positive number: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mi>sec</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to \pi/2^-} \sec x</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \infty</annotation></semantics></math>. From the right, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos x</annotation></semantics></math> is small and negative, and the limit is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\infty</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Right: the reciprocal of a small positive number is large and positive.
That is the behavior from the right, where cosine is negative.
Cosine approaches <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>; its reciprocal grows without bound instead.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sec</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sec 0 = 1</annotation></semantics></math> is the bottom of the branch, not its behavior near the asymptote.

why.correct: On <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos x</annotation></semantics></math> falls from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> toward <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> and stays positive. Dividing <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> by smaller and smaller positive numbers gives larger and larger results, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sec</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sec x</annotation></semantics></math> increases from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> without bound.
options: Right: a shrinking positive denominator makes the reciprocal grow.
A reciprocal moves the opposite way: as the positive cosine decreases, the secant increases.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos x</annotation></semantics></math> decreases on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>; it goes from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>.

Being positive and less than <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> makes secant greater than <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>; it does not say whether secant rises or falls.

why.correct: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>csc</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\csc\frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{\sin(\pi/4)}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}/2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \sqrt{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cot</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cot\frac{\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\cos(\pi/6)}{\sin(\pi/6)}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\sqrt{3}/2}{1/2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \sqrt{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 0</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sec</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>0</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sec\frac{\pi}{2} = \frac{1}{0}</annotation></semantics></math> is undefined. The others divide by a sine, which is not <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> at these angles.
options: Right: secant divides by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cot</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cot\frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\cos(\pi/2)}{\sin(\pi/2)}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{0}{1}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 0</annotation></semantics></math>: zero on top is fine.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>csc</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>1</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\csc\frac{\pi}{2} = \frac{1}{1} = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>csc</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\csc\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{1}{1/2} = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>csc</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\csc\theta = \frac{1}{\sin\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> takes the values <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>. Sine increases, so its reciprocal decreases, from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Right: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>></mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>></mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>></mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2 > \sqrt{2} > \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3} > 1</annotation></semantics></math>.
Those are the sine values; cosecant is their reciprocal.
The order is reversed: as sine grows, cosecant shrinks.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>csc</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\csc\frac{\pi}{2} = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>; cosecant never takes values between <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>csc</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos x \csc x</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \cos x \cdot \frac{1}{\sin x}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>cot</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \cot x</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>csc</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan x \csc x</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\sin x}{\cos x} \cdot \frac{1}{\sin x}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{\cos x}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>sec</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \sec x</annotation></semantics></math> (where <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin x \ne 0</annotation></semantics></math>).

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>csc</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\csc x = \frac{1}{\sin x}</annotation></semantics></math> has asymptotes where <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>, at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = k\pi</annotation></semantics></math>. On the open interval <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0, 2\pi)</annotation></semantics></math> that is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \pi</annotation></semantics></math> alone; <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi</annotation></semantics></math> are excluded.
options: Yes: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\pi = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

No: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\frac{\pi}{2} = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>csc</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\csc\frac{\pi}{2} = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, a turning point.

No: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\frac{3\pi}{2} = -1</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>csc</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\csc\frac{3\pi}{2} = -1</annotation></semantics></math>, a turning point.

No: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>csc</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\csc\frac{\pi}{4} = \sqrt{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, a defined value.

why.correct: Cotangent, like tangent, has period <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>. With <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b = 2</annotation></semantics></math> the period is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Right: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{|b|} = \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, using the sine rule; cotangent repeats every <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, so divide <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>.
Cotangent already repeats every <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, before any change.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b = 2</annotation></semantics></math> shortens the period; it does not lengthen it.

why.correct: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\frac{5\pi}{6} = -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sec</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sec\frac{5\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{-\sqrt{3}/2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cot</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cot x = \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}</annotation></semantics></math> takes every real value on each branch, falling from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\infty</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\infty</annotation></semantics></math> between consecutive zeros of sine.
options: Right: each branch of cotangent passes through every real number.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sec</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sec x</annotation></semantics></math> never takes values strictly between <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>csc</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\csc x</annotation></semantics></math> never takes values strictly between <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos x</annotation></semantics></math> stays in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-1, 1]</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: Sine rises, so its reciprocal falls; the period of cosecant stays <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi</annotation></semantics></math>.

variables.name: sin x
variables.why: Sine increases on the first quadrant, from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

variables.name: csc x
variables.why: Cosecant is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{\sin x}</annotation></semantics></math>, and dividing by a growing positive number gives a smaller result: from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

variables.name: The period of csc x
variables.why: The period is a property of the whole function, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi</annotation></semantics></math>, and does not depend on where you look along the graph.

why.correct: One form of the double-angle identity is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos(2x) = 1 - 2\sin^2 x</annotation></semantics></math>. The graph agrees: it starts at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>, reaches <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> and repeats every <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Right: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 - 2\sin^2 x</annotation></semantics></math> is one of the three forms of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos(2x)</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos^2 x</annotation></semantics></math> is never negative, but the graph goes down to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin(2x)</annotation></semantics></math> starts at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>; the graph starts at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>.
