<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>tan</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>sec</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 + \tan^2 x = \sec^2 x</annotation></semantics></math> (divide <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1</annotation></semantics></math> by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos^2 x</annotation></semantics></math>). Then <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sec</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sec^2 x\cos x</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{\cos^2 x}\cdot\cos x</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{\cos x}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>sec</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \sec x</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\left(x - \frac{\pi}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \cos x\cos\frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \sin x\sin\frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \cos x\cdot 0</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \sin x\cdot 1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \sin x</annotation></semantics></math>. Cosine shifted right <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> is sine.
options: Right: the cosine term drops out because <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

The cosine difference identity adds: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos a\cos b + \sin a\sin b</annotation></semantics></math>.

The <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos x</annotation></semantics></math> term is multiplied by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\frac{\pi}{2} = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

The surviving term is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin x\sin\frac{\pi}{2} = \sin x</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: The Pythagorean identity and its forms, and the double-angle identity for cosine, hold everywhere. Doubling an angle does not double its sine, and the sine of a sum is not the sum of the sines.
options: Identity: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1</annotation></semantics></math> rearranged.

Not an identity: at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\pi = 0</annotation></semantics></math> but <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\sin\frac{\pi}{2} = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.
Identity: one form of the double-angle identity.

Not an identity: at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = y = \frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\pi = 0</annotation></semantics></math> but the right side is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>.

Identity: divide <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1</annotation></semantics></math> by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos^2 x</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\sin x\cos x = \sin x</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\sin x\cos x - \sin x = 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin x(2\cos x - 1) = 0</annotation></semantics></math>. Either <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin x = 0</annotation></semantics></math> (<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0, \pi</annotation></semantics></math>) or <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos x = \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> (<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \frac{\pi}{3}, \frac{5\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>).
options: Right: factor out <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin x</annotation></semantics></math> and solve both factors.

Dividing by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin x</annotation></semantics></math> loses <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \pi</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

These come from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin x = 0</annotation></semantics></math> alone; the factor <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\cos x - 1</annotation></semantics></math> gives two more.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\frac{2\pi}{3} = -\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>; the second angle with cosine <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{5\pi}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3} - \frac{\pi}{4}\right)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \cos\frac{\pi}{3}\cos\frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \sin\frac{\pi}{3}\sin\frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">+</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mn>6</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{6}}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos^2 x - \sin^2 x</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \cos(2x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2\cos^2 x - 1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2\cdot\frac{1}{9} - 1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -\frac{7}{9}</annotation></semantics></math>. Directly: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin^2 x = 1 - \frac{1}{9} = \frac{8}{9}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{9} - \frac{8}{9} = -\frac{7}{9}</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Right: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\cos^2 x - 1</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos^2 x = \frac{1}{9}</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\cos x - 1</annotation></semantics></math>: the cosine was not squared.

The sign is reversed: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{9} - \frac{8}{9}</annotation></semantics></math> is negative.

That uses <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin^2 x = \frac{2}{9}</annotation></semantics></math>; from the Pythagorean identity, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin^2 x = 1 - \frac{1}{9} = \frac{8}{9}</annotation></semantics></math>.

why.correct: Q is on the circle of radius <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>, on the ray <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{5\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math> (five steps of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math> from the polar axis). Polar coordinates list the distance first, then the angle: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(2, \frac{5\pi}{6}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>.
options: Right: distance <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>, angle <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{5\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The order is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(r, \theta)</annotation></semantics></math>: distance first, then angle.

why.correct: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> is negative and decreasing, so its size, the distance from the origin, increases.

variables.why: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math> goes from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 2\sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math> goes from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2</annotation></semantics></math>.

variables.name: The distance from the origin to the point
variables.why: The distance is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|r|</annotation></semantics></math>, which grows from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> as <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> becomes more negative.

why.correct: With <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r > 0</annotation></semantics></math>, the distance from the origin is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>. A negative average rate of change means <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo><</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(b) < r(a)</annotation></semantics></math>: overall, the distance shrinks by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.5</annotation></semantics></math> units for each radian the angle turns.
options: Right: negative rate with positive <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> means a shrinking distance.
The rate is negative and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> is positive, so the distance decreases.
A rate of change describes change per radian, not a position.

The angle increases from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math>; the rate is change in <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> per radian.

why.correct: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 2 + 2\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math> is never negative. It is largest, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\theta = 1</annotation></semantics></math> (<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = 0</annotation></semantics></math>), and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> where <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\theta = -1</annotation></semantics></math> (<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \pi</annotation></semantics></math>).
options: Right: the extremes of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> give the farthest and closest points.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\pi = -1</annotation></semantics></math> makes <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 0</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>; the maximum is at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 2</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> is not the largest value, and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r = 0</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta = \pi</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>.
